themes.label: Discovery and search
themes.complaint_title: I cannot find the thing I know exists
themes.complaint_body: Search and browsing return the wrong projects, or nothing, and there is no way to tell why. Finding a project by the problem it solves -- rather than by its name -- does not work.

themes.label: Onboarding and first steps
themes.complaint_title: I do not know what to do first here
themes.complaint_body: A newcomer lands on the site and cannot tell what the first useful action is: which page to read, what a complaint is, or how to contribute a fifteen-minute task.

themes.label: Complaint quality
themes.complaint_title: Complaints are vague, duplicated or impossible to act on
themes.complaint_body: Reports arrive without reproduction steps, restate each other, or name a symptom nobody can reproduce, so validating them is guesswork and the good ones are lost in the noise.

themes.label: Feature proposals and planning
themes.complaint_title: The backlog proposes things without evidence or cost
themes.complaint_body: Features are filed without a linked complaint, without a size anyone can interpret, and without showing what they would displace, so the roadmap is a pile rather than a plan.

themes.label: Consensus and governance
themes.complaint_title: Decisions stall, or get made by whoever is loudest
themes.complaint_body: Calls sit below quorum for weeks, voters miss deadlines in other timezones, and a contested decision leaves no record of why the minority disagreed.

themes.label: Trust and reputation
themes.complaint_title: Reputation is a black box and easy to game
themes.complaint_body: Nobody can see how their weight was computed, activity counts the same as accuracy, and a long history becomes a permanent advantage nobody can challenge.

themes.label: Moderation and abuse
themes.complaint_title: Abuse has no proportionate response
themes.complaint_body: The only tools are a report box and a ban. Low-grade harassment, coordinated voting and spam from throwaway accounts have nothing between 'ignore it' and 'remove the person'.

themes.label: Notifications
themes.complaint_title: I miss what matters and get pinged for noise
themes.complaint_body: Everything is either silent or a broadcast. There is no digest, no per-project control, and no notification when the complaint I filed is validated or the fix ships.

themes.label: Feeds and syndication
themes.complaint_title: Progress is invisible from outside the site
themes.complaint_body: Following a project means visiting it. There is no usable feed, no per-decision subscription, and nothing for a reader who does not want an account.

themes.label: Documents and knowledge
themes.complaint_title: Knowledge lives in threads and is never written down
themes.complaint_body: Specs are documents nobody links to, decisions are rows nobody reads, and the same explanation is given again every few months in a comment.

themes.label: Requests from the outside
themes.complaint_title: What users ask for never reaches the roadmap
themes.complaint_body: Requests arrive in a form, disappear into a list, and are answered by hand if at all; there is no count of who wants what and no honest 'we are not doing this'.

themes.label: Project health and metrics
themes.complaint_title: Project health is unmeasured or misleading
themes.complaint_body: The health score shows a number with no components, 'no data' renders as zero, and a project that died six months ago still looks fine in a list.

themes.label: Data portability and exit
themes.complaint_title: Leaving with my data is hard
themes.complaint_body: There is no export, no documented format, and no way to verify that a backup can be restored. What I contributed here is only readable here.

themes.label: Accessibility and language
themes.complaint_title: The site excludes people who need accessibility or another language
themes.complaint_body: Keyboard traversal is inconsistent, focus is not always visible, there is no second language, and nothing checks contrast or announcements in CI.

themes.label: Performance
themes.complaint_title: Pages and search are slow
themes.complaint_body: The project page loads six panels at once, search re-queries on every keystroke, and no budget stops the JavaScript from growing release by release.

themes.label: Security and privacy
themes.complaint_title: Security and privacy are bolted on
themes.complaint_body: There is no second factor, no session list, no CSRF token discipline and no way to see who read a private project; secrets and backups are handled by convention.

themes.label: Integrations with where the work happens
themes.complaint_title: Work happens elsewhere and never reaches this site
themes.complaint_body: Commits, pull requests and CI live in a forge, discussion lives here, and nothing connects them: status is retyped by hand.

themes.label: Mobile use
themes.complaint_title: The site is unusable on a phone
themes.complaint_body: Primary controls are out of thumb reach, the board scrolls sideways, text is small, and there is no offline reading, no install, and no mobile test in CI.

themes.label: Interface depth
themes.complaint_title: The interface is thin and repetitive
themes.complaint_body: Every panel is a list with a button. Empty states are blank, destructive actions ask for confirmation instead of offering undo, and there is no command palette or comparison view.

themes.label: Assisted editorial work
themes.complaint_title: Repetitive editorial work is manual
themes.complaint_body: Grouping duplicates, drafting a complaint from a title, summarising a long thread and translating a report are all done by hand, badly and late.

themes.label: Federation and portability of the network
themes.complaint_title: This project is an island
themes.complaint_body: Nothing here is visible to the wider web except as a web page: no ActivityPub, no WebFinger, no static mirror, no way for another instance to describe the same project.

themes.label: Measurement
themes.complaint_title: Nobody can see whether any of this works
themes.complaint_body: There is no funnel, no lead time, no retention, no search success rate: the instance cannot say whether a change helped.

themes.label: Community and retention
themes.complaint_title: Contributors have no reason to stay
themes.complaint_body: Credit goes to the author only, there is no portfolio, no mentorship that reaches a person, and no public thank-you that is not a badge.

themes.label: The project's own quality
themes.complaint_title: The project's own quality is unverified
themes.complaint_body: Claims in the docs drift from the code, there is no status page, no incident log, no fuzzing and no measured restore; the gates exist but nobody publishes their scores.

themes.label: Intake: ideas without an invented complaint
themes.complaint_title: I have to invent a complaint to record an idea
themes.complaint_body: Every feature must trace to a validated complaint. A project that wants to collect ideas before anyone has suffered from anything must therefore file fictional pain: the complaint becomes a formality written to satisfy a validator, and the feature list fills with invented problems.

themes.label: Milestones: grouping what is being planned
themes.complaint_title: I cannot group the ideas I am planning into one milestone
themes.complaint_body: Phases live in board_columns and themes live in tags, so a plan exists only as prose in a PLAN file. The instance cannot answer which ideas belong to the release a maintainer is working towards, so a hundred and thirty drafted ideas read as one undifferentiated pile.

themes.label: Roadmap: planned versus merely filed
themes.complaint_title: I cannot tell what is planned from what is merely written down
themes.complaint_body: A draft feature means somebody had the idea. Nothing on the instance distinguishes it from a commitment, so the roadmap exists in a document, drifts from the page, and no reader can see what is coming without opening a repository.

themes.label: Scheduling: what blocks what
themes.complaint_title: Grouping is not scheduling: I cannot say what blocks what
themes.complaint_body: A milestone's contents can be listed but not ordered, because nothing records that one idea must land before another. WIP limits exist per phase and dependencies do not exist at all, so a plan that is real in somebody's head cannot be expressed on the board.

discovery.title: Rank search results by complaint pain, not recency
discovery.body: A search for 'export' should surface the project whose complaint volume says export is its worst problem, not the project that edited its description yesterday. The scorer already has pain scores; the search ORDER BY does not read them.

discovery.title: Explain every search result's rank in one click
discovery.body: Each hit gets a 'why this?' disclosure listing the terms that matched, the pain score, the arena standing and the health term with their weights, so a surprising order is diagnosable instead of mysterious.

discovery.title: Search inside complaint and feature bodies, not just titles
discovery.body: Full-text is already indexed for entities; the query parser only admits titles in some paths. Unified search over title+body with match highlighting per field.

discovery.title: Saved searches with a diff feed
discovery.body: Persist a query and a baseline result set; the feed then reports 'three projects entered, one left, two moved up' since the last visit instead of a static list.

discovery.title: Faceted search over governance model, license and language at once
discovery.body: The facet SQL exists per dimension; a combined facet panel with counts that update as each filter narrows, and a 'no results because of X' breakdown when the intersection is empty.

discovery.title: A 'similar projects' panel built from the embedding index
discovery.body: Every entity already has an embedding; project-level similarity is one aggregation away and gives a reader a way out of a dead end without a second search.

discovery.title: Search that understands complaints as queries
discovery.body: Type a sentence of pain ('I cannot tell which call was decided') and get ranked features that answer it, with the complaint text used as the query rather than keywords.

discovery.title: Zero-result recovery with query rewriting
discovery.body: On no hits: drop the rarest term, then the filter with the smallest population, and say which one was dropped. Today a zero result is a dead end.

discovery.title: Taxonomy-guided browse that shows population before you click
discovery.body: Every taxonomy node carries a live count; a node with zero members is visibly empty rather than a link to an empty page.

discovery.title: Pinned 'start here' paths per intent
discovery.body: Curated three-step journeys (evaluate, contribute, complain) assembled from real routes, stored as data so they can be edited without a deploy.

discovery.title: Cross-project duplicate detection at proposal time
discovery.body: When a feature is filed, the similarity search runs instance-wide and tells the filer which other project already ships it, with a link.

discovery.title: A public sitemap of every project's surfaces
discovery.body: Human-readable and machine-readable (/sitemap.xml), generated from the router so a new page cannot be invisible to crawlers.

discovery.title: Search analytics that never store the searcher
discovery.body: Count queries, zero-result rate and click-through per term with a k-anonymity floor, so the catalog can be improved without logging who searched.

onboarding.title: A first-session checklist generated from real state
onboarding.body: Four steps (read a complaint, vote on a pair, claim a task, file a complaint) where each is checked by querying the database, not by a client-side flag.

onboarding.title: A 'your first hour' guided tour built from the contribution feed
onboarding.body: One route that walks a newcomer from their language to a 15-minute task, using the feed's own ranking so the tour cannot recommend something the feed would not.

onboarding.title: Explain the complaint-first rule in the place it bites
onboarding.body: The feature form already refuses an unlinked feature; inline it with a one-paragraph rationale and a 'file the complaint first' link that preserves what was typed.

onboarding.title: Sample data in a scratch project a newcomer can break
onboarding.body: A sandbox project, seeded with a small governance history, that accepts votes and claims from anyone and is excluded from every public ranking.

onboarding.title: Pair a newcomer with a mentor from the task's own field
onboarding.body: Work items already carry needs_mentor; a mentor opt-in on the profile turns that flag into an actual name and a channel, instead of a label.

onboarding.title: A per-project 'what this place is for' paragraph an owner writes
onboarding.body: The description is a tagline today; a longer intent statement, rendered above the complaint box, is what stops off-topic filings.

onboarding.title: Onboarding email that arrives only after a real action
onboarding.body: Send the welcome after the first vote or complaint, not at signup, so it can reference what the person actually did.

onboarding.title: Keyboard-first navigation with a discoverable cheat sheet
onboarding.body: A '?' overlay listing every shortcut, generated from the same table the handlers use so it cannot drift.

onboarding.title: A glossary of Concord's own vocabulary
onboarding.body: Complaint, validated, ratified, quorum, override window, arena, field report: each defined once, linked inline with a tooltip from every use.

onboarding.title: Show the trust ladder with the next rung's requirement
onboarding.body: A member sees what their current role permits and exactly what would raise it, computed from the same rules the guard enforces.

onboarding.title: A 'what changed since you last looked' strip on the home page
onboarding.body: One line per project the visitor follows, summarising the decisions since their last visit rather than a wall of timestamps.

onboarding.title: Interactive example of a consensus decision
onboarding.body: A replayable toy call with five voters where the reader can change a vote and watch quorum, block and override behave, using the real governance package compiled to WASM or mirrored in JS from the same test vectors.

onboarding.title: Refuse nothing silently: every disabled control says why
onboarding.body: A shared pattern for disabled buttons with the reason and the remedy inline, replacing the current mix of hidden and greyed-out controls.

complaint_quality.title: A rejection reason taxonomy instead of free text
complaint_quality.body: Rejecting a complaint currently writes a free-text note; a short fixed list (not reproducible, duplicate, not about this project, abuse) makes rejection patterns measurable and appealable.

complaint_quality.title: Merge duplicates instead of rejecting the second one
complaint_quality.body: A merge keeps both reporters' weight and links the survivor to both, so a popular complaint filed twice does not lose half its evidence.

complaint_quality.title: Ask for reproduction steps with a structured field
complaint_quality.body: Three optional fields (what you did, what happened, what you expected) that render as a blockquote on the complaint page and feed the embedding.

complaint_quality.title: Auto-draft the title from the body
complaint_quality.body: A filer who writes two sentences gets a suggested title they can edit; most vague titles come from writing the body last.

complaint_quality.title: A validation queue with the evidence summary inline
complaint_quality.body: The queue shows severity, frequency, reporter trust and similar existing complaints side by side, so validating takes one screen instead of four.

complaint_quality.title: Time-boxed validation with an escalation
complaint_quality.body: An open complaint older than N days is surfaced to the project's maintainers with the option to validate, reject or explicitly defer, so nothing rots in 'open'.

complaint_quality.title: Complaint clustering by embedding, with a canonical example
complaint_quality.body: Group near-identical complaints into a cluster whose page shows all reporters and the canonical wording, then let features link the cluster rather than one row.

complaint_quality.title: Severity calibrated against outcomes
complaint_quality.body: Compare the severity a reporter claimed with the impact the shipped fix had (field report rate); publish the calibration per reporter so severity stops being a free dial.

complaint_quality.title: Require a 'what I tried' field before a duplicate is claimed
complaint_quality.body: Duplicate detection is advisory; asking what the filer already searched turns a lazy duplicate into a genuine one or a search that failed, and the second is a bug.

complaint_quality.title: Complaint expiry for projects that stopped caring
complaint_quality.body: A complaint untouched for a year on an archived project is marked stale rather than open, so instance-wide pain scores are not inflated by abandoned projects.

complaint_quality.title: A public complaint quality score per project
complaint_quality.body: Ratio of validated to rejected to stale, with the same n-always rule as the other metrics, so a project that rejects everything is visible.

complaint_quality.title: Link complaints to the exact surface that hurt
complaint_quality.body: An optional path field (/projects/{slug}/board) recorded when the complaint is filed from that page, which makes the pain locatable and the fix testable.

complaint_quality.title: Report a complaint's resolution back to its reporters
complaint_quality.body: When a feature linked to a complaint ships, every reporter gets one notification with the diff, closing the loop that otherwise ends at 'validated'.

feature_planning.title: A cost model that turns effort sizes into hours
feature_planning.body: S/M/L/XL is a label nobody can compare; a per-project table calibrating each size to a median actual, derived from claim-to-close time, makes the sizes mean something.

feature_planning.title: Automatic impact estimate from the linked complaints' pain
feature_planning.body: When a feature links a complaint, prefill impact with the complaint's pain score band, marked as a suggestion the author can override with a reason.

feature_planning.title: Show what a feature would displace
feature_planning.body: Every proposal ranked by the board is really a claim on the same capacity; a panel showing 'this is above N other ready features' makes the trade-off explicit at filing time.

feature_planning.title: Split a feature into work items at proposal time
feature_planning.body: The work-item contract exists but is filled after the fact; a template with three sub-tasks on creation turns a proposal into something a newcomer can claim on day one.

feature_planning.title: A 'what would have to be true' field for speculative features
feature_planning.body: One optional line stating the assumption that makes the feature worth building, surfaced again when the feature is picked up, so dead assumptions are noticed rather than inherited.

feature_planning.title: Reject features whose every linked complaint is stale
feature_planning.body: A cheap guard: if all linked complaints are stale or rejected, the feature drops to the backlog with that reason instead of ranking on dead pain.

feature_planning.title: Estimate confidence, not just impact
feature_planning.body: A three-point (low/likely/high) impact estimate per feature, shown as a spread; a single number hides the disagreement that matters most.

feature_planning.title: A dependency field between features
feature_planning.body: Features can block each other; declaring it lets the board show a critical path and stops a feature being claimed before its prerequisite ships.

feature_planning.title: Auto-close features superseded by a shipped one
feature_planning.body: When a feature ships, the similarity search runs over the remaining backlog and proposes supersede links for review, so the backlog does not keep proposing what exists.

feature_planning.title: Public 'why not' notes on rejected features
feature_planning.body: A rejected feature keeps a one-paragraph rationale visible at its own URL, so the same idea is not re-filed every quarter by someone who never saw the first discussion.

feature_planning.title: Board view grouped by complaint theme
feature_planning.body: The board is a flat list by status; grouping by the theme of the linked complaints shows whether the roadmap is coherent or nineteen unrelated things.

feature_planning.title: Cycle-time forecast from the last N deliveries
feature_planning.body: Median time from ready to shipped, per effort size, rendered as 'this is likely to land in about three weeks' with its sample size.

feature_planning.title: A 'smallest version' field enforced by a lint
feature_planning.body: Every XL feature must name a smaller version that delivers part of the value; a lint refuses to mark it ready otherwise. XL features are where backlogs go to die.

consensus.title: Quorum targets shown live on every open call
consensus.body: The consensus page states the rule; a countdown to quorum ('4 of 7 needed, 2 unreachable') turns a stalled call into an actionable one.

consensus.title: Nudge the people whose vote would decide a call
consensus.body: When a call is one vote from quorum, notify exactly the members who have not voted, once, with the deadline — not a broadcast.

consensus.title: A written minority report attached to every ratified decision
consensus.body: Objections are counted today; capturing the strongest dissent verbatim (one optional paragraph per objector) preserves the reasoning that the tally destroys.

consensus.title: Decision records exported as readable documents
consensus.body: The decision record exists as rows; render it as a one-page markdown document with the alternatives, the tally, the dissent and the date, and link it from the feature.

consensus.title: Re-open a decided call when its assumptions break
consensus.body: A superseded decision can be reopened by citing the changed fact, with quorum on the reopen rather than on the original question.

consensus.title: Weight votes by participation history, with the rule stated
consensus.body: A member who has voted on 90% of calls should not weigh the same as one who votes on 5%, as long as the rule is published, ratifiable and visible on the call.

consensus.title: Time-zone aware voting windows
consensus.body: Show the close time in the reader's own zone and guarantee at least one round-the-clock period, so a call cannot close while half the voters sleep.

consensus.title: Abstentions that carry a reason
consensus.body: An abstain is currently a non-vote; letting it carry 'I lack context on X' routes real information to the proposer and distinguishes indifference from ignorance.

consensus.title: Consensus health over time per project
consensus.body: Median time to quorum, share of calls decided by override, share closed at deadline: three numbers that diagnose a governance process better than any single vote.

consensus.title: Simulate a proposal's likely fate before filing
consensus.body: Given the current membership and recent voting patterns, show the quorum it would need and the blocks it would attract, as a forecast explicitly labelled a forecast.

consensus.title: Delegation with a public ledger
consensus.body: A member may delegate their vote on a theme to someone else; the delegation and its revocation are both audited and shown on every call it affects.

consensus.title: Emergency holds that expire by default
consensus.body: An operator hold exists; give it a mandatory expiry and a written justification, so a hold cannot quietly become a decision.

consensus.title: A 'consensus' page that teaches by example from this instance
consensus.body: Render three real closed calls (one unanimous, one contested, one overridden) as case studies with the tallies that decided them.

trust.title: One page per member: what they did, what it earned
trust.body: Reputation events exist as rows; a profile that lists them with the points each carried makes the score auditable instead of a mystery number.

trust.title: Decay reputation that is never exercised
trust.body: A vote cast three years ago should not still weigh; an explicit half-life with the rule published, and the decayed value shown beside the raw one.

trust.title: Cap the weight a single member can hold
trust.body: A hard ceiling with the excess redistributed proportionally, so a long history cannot become a permanent veto.

trust.title: Publish the reputation curve as a chart, not a formula
trust.body: The formula is in the code; a rendered curve with the reader's own position marked is what makes it understandable.

trust.title: Separate accuracy from activity
trust.body: Two scores: how often a member's predictions were right (validation accuracy, field-report accuracy) and how much they do. Conflating them rewards volume.

trust.title: Dispute a reputation event with evidence
trust.body: Every negative event is appealable once, with the appeal and its outcome recorded on the member's page and visible to whoever set the role.

trust.title: Trust grants that expire
trust.body: Granting contributor rights for a project can carry an expiry, so access granted for one release does not become permanent by inattention.

trust.title: A 'trusted by' panel on the project page
trust.body: Who vouched for this project, and when, drawn from actual grants rather than membership count.

trust.title: Sybil resistance for guest accounts without an email
trust.body: Guest contributions can be cheap to farm; a proof-of-work stamp or a rate that scales with account age, stated plainly at signup.

trust.title: Field-report weight tied to demonstrated skill
trust.body: A report from someone who has shipped in the area counts more than one from a passer-by, computed from their own shipped work and published.

trust.title: A public log of every role change
trust.body: Who promoted whom, with the reason field mandatory, in the audit ledger's existing format — promotion is the highest-leverage admin action and the least documented today.

trust.title: Revocation that explains itself to the revoked
trust.body: Losing a role currently just changes what buttons work; a notification with the rule and the path to appeal.

trust.title: Reputation portability across projects on the instance
trust.body: A member's accuracy on one project informs their starting weight on another, bounded so a bad first project cannot follow them forever.

safety.title: A graduated response ladder with published thresholds
safety.body: Warn, then limit, then require review, then suspend: each step with a stated trigger and a time bound, so moderation is a policy rather than a mood.

safety.title: Shadow-limit instead of ban for low-severity abuse
safety.body: The abuser keeps posting and sees their own content; nobody else does. Removes the incentive to sock-puppet while a review happens.

safety.title: Report categories that route to different queues
safety.body: Spam, off-topic, harassment, illegal and security go to different people with different deadlines, instead of one undifferentiated report box.

safety.title: A reviewer-facing evidence bundle
safety.body: One page per report: the content, the history of the reporter and the reported, prior reports, and the action taken last time — so decisions are consistent.

safety.title: Appeals with an independent second reviewer
safety.body: An appeal goes to somebody who did not make the first decision, and the fact that they were independent is recorded.

safety.title: Rate-limit by behaviour, not just by IP
safety.body: Bursts of near-identical text, many accounts from one browser fingerprint and rapid role-change attempts are the shapes that matter; IP limits catch almost none of them.

safety.title: Content warnings on complaints about third parties
safety.body: A complaint that names a person can be filed with a warning flag, so the page does not broadcast an accusation as its first impression.

safety.title: Delete-with-tombstone instead of hard delete
safety.body: Deleted content leaves a row saying what was deleted and why, so threads and audit trails do not develop holes that look like tampering.

safety.title: A transparency report generated from the audit ledger
safety.body: Actions per month by type, appeals upheld, and the median time to first response, computed from rows that already exist and published as a page.

safety.title: Keyword walls that explain themselves
safety.body: When a submission is refused for a blocked term, name the category rather than the word list, so a legitimate filer can adapt instead of guessing.

safety.title: Escalation on unanswered reports
safety.body: A report with no action within the policy window escalates to the next role automatically and appears in a queue nobody can miss.

safety.title: Self-service data removal on request
safety.body: A member can request removal of their own content; the request, the decision and the reason are recorded, and the outcome is a tombstone.

safety.title: Abuse-resistant voting on controversial calls
safety.body: Coordinated voting is hard to prove; requiring quorum diversity (distinct accounts older than N days) on calls flagged as contested is a cheap structural defence.

notifications.title: One digest per person per day, with a truthful count
notifications.body: Every event type currently competes for attention; a single daily digest ranked by relevance, and nothing else, except for direct mentions.

notifications.title: Per-project, per-event-type preferences that persist
notifications.body: A matrix of project × event (decision, ship, reply, mention) stored server-side, with a 'quiet project' switch that is one click.

notifications.title: Email that works without a client
notifications.body: A plain-text multipart alternative and a one-click unsubscribe that needs no login, because a digest nobody can leave is a spam folder waiting to happen.

notifications.title: Web push with a permission prompt that earns itself
notifications.body: Ask after the second visit and the first follow, never on load, and state what will be sent.

notifications.title: A notification when your complaint is validated, rejected or shipped
notifications.body: Three specific moments a reporter cares about; today the reporter learns nothing until they poll.

notifications.title: Do-not-disturb windows in the member's own timezone
notifications.body: A stated quiet window that holds non-urgent mail until it ends, with urgent (security, role change) exempt and marked.

notifications.title: An inbox that survives the device
notifications.body: Read state stored server-side, so the badge is the same on the phone and the laptop.

notifications.title: Batching for high-volume projects
notifications.body: A project with 200 watchers should not create 200 notification rows per event; fan out at read time from a single event.

notifications.title: Watch a specific feature, not a whole project
notifications.body: The useful granularity for most people is one decision, and the current model only offers the project.

notifications.title: Delivery diagnostics the member can see
notifications.body: A page listing what was sent, when, and whether it bounced, so 'I never got it' is answerable.

notifications.title: A weekly 'what you missed' that is skimmable in 30 seconds
notifications.body: Five bullets, each a real decision with its outcome, ordered by how much the reader's own votes mattered.

notifications.title: Notifications that link to the exact anchor
notifications.body: Every notification deep-links to the comment, tally or diff it refers to, not to the project root.

notifications.title: Suppress notifications for your own actions
notifications.body: An author currently gets notified about their own edits on some paths; a single filter at emit time, with a test.

feeds.title: One RSS feed per project with full history
feeds.body: The feed item exists per decision; a proper Atom feed with stable IDs, pagination and an 'all history' variant lets readers follow without an account.

feeds.title: JSON Feed alongside RSS
feeds.body: The same items in JSON Feed 1.1, so scripts do not parse XML.

feeds.title: Per-feature feeds for long-running discussions
feeds.body: Someone following one contested decision should not have to follow the project.

feeds.title: WebSub or a ping endpoint for feed readers
feeds.body: Announce new items instead of polling, so a feed reader sees the update in minutes.

feeds.title: An instance-wide 'recently decided' feed
feeds.body: Across projects, what was ratified, overridden or blocked, with the tally — the single best signal that the instance is alive.

feeds.title: Feed items that carry the reasoning, not just the title
feeds.body: Include the winning argument's first paragraph and the vote split in the item body, so the reader can judge without clicking.

feeds.title: Stable feed IDs that survive a rename
feeds.body: IDs derived from the decision row, not the slug, so a project rename does not duplicate every item in every reader.

feeds.title: A monthly archive feed
feeds.body: One item per month summarising decisions and ships, for people who want to follow at low frequency.

feeds.title: Conditional GET and ETags on every feed
feeds.body: Feed readers poll constantly; a correct 304 keeps a tunnel's bandwidth honest.

feeds.title: Feeds for a saved search
feeds.body: Follow a query rather than a project: 'everything matching export in any project'.

feeds.title: A 'why this item is in your feed' line
feeds.body: Each item states the subscription that produced it, which makes a noisy feed diagnosable.

feeds.title: Atom categories from the taxonomy
feeds.body: Tag every item with its theme so a reader can filter without a full-text rule.

feeds.title: Feed discovery from the HTML head
feeds.body: Every page advertises its relevant feed with a link rel=alternate, so a reader extension can find it.

documents.title: Docs that are versioned with the code, not in a wiki
documents.body: The documents surface exists; bind a document to a path in a repository and show a diff when it changes, so the spec and the code cannot drift silently.

documents.title: Inline anchors for every spec section
documents.body: Stable permalinks per heading, and every reference elsewhere (issues, decisions, code comments) can cite §section as a link rather than a string.

documents.title: A 'this spec is stale' flag computed from code churn
documents.body: When the files a spec covers change more than N times without the spec changing, mark it visibly stale on its own page.

documents.title: Decision records linked from the code they explain
documents.body: A comment convention (a decision URL) that the linter checks, so a non-obvious branch points at the reasoning instead of at a ticket.

documents.title: A glossary that is also a schema
documents.body: One YAML file of terms; the glossary page, the tooltips and the lint that rejects undefined jargon all read it.

documents.title: Architecture diagrams generated from the module graph
documents.body: Render the import graph with the layering rules annotated, so a violated dependency shows as a crossing arrow rather than a review comment.

documents.title: A changelog assembled from shipped features
documents.body: Each ship event already has a title and a body; group by week and project into a public changelog with no extra authoring.

documents.title: Docs search that searches code too
documents.body: One box that returns both spec sections and the symbols they describe.

documents.title: Markdown linting in CI with the project's own rules
documents.body: Enforce heading order, link validity and a maximum ratio of prose to examples, and fail the build on a broken internal link.

documents.title: A 'how this project decides' one-pager per governance model
documents.body: Generated from the governance package's parameters, so a model change updates the explanation automatically.

documents.title: Commentable specs with consensus on the paragraph
documents.body: A spec paragraph can be attached to a call; the decision cites the paragraph and the paragraph shows the decision's state inline.

documents.title: Doc ownership with a reviewer field
documents.body: Each document names an owner who is notified when it changes, ending the 'everybody's document' problem.

documents.title: Export a project's whole documentation as one PDF or EPUB
documents.body: One command produces a readable artifact with a table of contents, for readers who do not read on the site.

requests.title: Requests that can be promoted to complaints in one click
requests.body: A user ask that many people repeat is a complaint with evidence; the promotion copies the thread and links the raised hands as frequency.

requests.title: Public counts of who wants a request
requests.body: A +1 that is a real relationship row rather than a counter, so the count is attributable and retractable.

requests.title: Request status that mirrors the roadmap automatically
requests.body: When a linked feature moves to ready or ships, the request's status follows, so nobody answers the same ask by hand.

requests.title: A monthly 'requests we are not doing, and why' page
requests.body: Saying no in public, once, with a reason per request, is cheaper than refusing the same ask twelve times.

requests.title: Requests from inside a project page, with the current page attached
requests.body: The most common request is 'this particular screen is wrong'; capture the URL automatically so the request is locatable.

requests.title: Anonymous requests with a reply channel
requests.body: A guest can file without an account and still get an answer, via a ticket URL that works like a reply address.

requests.title: Cluster requests by embedding, show the cluster
requests.body: Ten asks about export are one ask; the cluster page is the thing the roadmap links to.

requests.title: A response-time promise, measured and displayed
requests.body: State 'we answer requests within five days' and show the actual median next to it, including when it is bad.

requests.title: Requests that expire with a re-ask
requests.body: An unanswered request older than a quarter closes with an apology and a 'still want this?' that reopens it with the new signal.

requests.title: Route requests by theme to the people who own the area
requests.body: A theme owner gets the request instead of a shared inbox, and the routing rule is visible on the form.

requests.title: Show the requester what happened to their ask, unprompted
requests.body: One email at the moment the outcome is known — built, declined, deferred — not a dashboard they have to remember to check.

requests.title: A billing-style statement of what the maintainers did this month
requests.body: Hours spent, decisions made, ships landed: the answer to 'is anyone home?' that a request board alone cannot give.

requests.title: Requests importable from email and chat
requests.body: A forwarding address that turns a message into a request with the sender's consent recorded.

health.title: Show the health score's components on the project page
health.body: The breakdown exists in the package and the search UI shows a bar; the project page should show recency, responsiveness, breadth and cadence with their weights and unknowns.

health.title: A health history sparkline from the snapshots
health.body: Once R15 lands, a 90-day line per component makes 'this project is dying' visible before it is dead.

health.title: Distinguish 'no data' from 'bad' everywhere health appears
health.body: One shared badge component with an unknown state, replacing the current mix of dashes, zeros and absent chips.

health.title: Health thresholds that trigger an automatic flag
health.body: A project whose recency drops below a stated line for a stated period gets a public 'needs maintainer' banner, not a silent score.

health.title: Bus factor from commit concentration
health.body: A single number: the share of recent commits by the top author, with the measurement stated, because the honest answer to 'who would leave' is usually one person.

health.title: Issue-response time as its own metric
health.body: Review latency is measured; first response to an issue is the number a user actually feels.

health.title: Dependency freshness
health.body: Share of declared dependencies within one major of current, with the sources and the check date published.

health.title: Test and CI signal imported from the forge
health.body: Passing rate and time-to-green over the last 30 runs, if the repository exposes it.

health.title: A public methodology page with the exact formula
health.body: Every component, weight and cut-off on one page, versioned, so a disputed score can be recomputed by hand.

health.title: Score a project's documentation, not just its code
health.body: Does it have a README with install steps, a changelog, an architecture note? Measured mechanically and stated as a checklist.

health.title: Compare a project against its own history, not the instance
health.body: An absolute score ranks projects against each other; the useful question for a maintainer is whether this month beat last month.

health.title: Let a maintainer dispute a metric with evidence
health.body: A disputed component is shown as disputed with the counter-evidence attached, rather than silently overriding the number.

health.title: Health for projects with no repository, derived from site activity
health.body: Sixty-nine catalog entries have no forge; decisions, complaints and ships are still measurable signals of life.

portability.title: A one-click full export of a project's data
portability.body: Complaints, features, votes, decisions, documents and audit in a documented JSON layout, zipped, streamed, with a checksum — the honest counter to a walled garden.

portability.title: Import that round-trips the export
portability.body: An export nobody can re-import is a backup, not portability; a test that exports, wipes a scratch instance and re-imports, comparing counts and IDs.

portability.title: A stable, versioned data format
portability.body: Ship the export with a schema version and a migration note per change, so a third-party tool can rely on it.

portability.title: Public read API without authentication
portability.body: Everything a logged-out reader can see should be readable by a script, with documented rate limits and pagination.

portability.title: A data retention policy the database enforces
portability.body: A stated window per table with a job that applies it, so 'we keep everything forever' is a decision rather than an accident.

portability.title: Export a single thread as a readable document
portability.body: Any complaint or call exports as markdown with its full history, for quoting outside the site.

portability.title: Account deletion that actually deletes
portability.body: An honest deletion path: what is removed, what is tombstoned, what is retained for audit and for how long, stated before the confirmation button.

portability.title: Downloadable audit ledger per project
portability.body: The ledger is the trust anchor; it should be exportable and independently verifiable (hash chain), not just viewable.

portability.title: A documented webhook event schema
portability.body: Consumers need to know the shapes before they subscribe; publish the JSON schema with versioning and a changelog.

portability.title: Data portability for reputation
portability.body: A signed statement of a member's contribution record they can present elsewhere, with the caveat that it is only as good as this instance's word.

portability.title: Backups documented and restore-tested
portability.body: A written restore procedure with a measured restore time, exercised on a schedule — the difference between a backup and a hope.

portability.title: A tombstone registry for deleted projects
portability.body: A deleted project keeps a URL explaining that it existed and when, so old links do not 404 into silence.

portability.title: Legal pages generated from configuration
portability.body: Privacy, terms and licence pages whose factual claims (what is stored, how long) are read from the same config the code uses.

a11y_i18n.title: An axe-core gate on every page in CI
a11y_i18n.body: The browser suites already run Playwright; an accessibility assertion per page turns 'we care about a11y' into a build failure.

a11y_i18n.title: Full keyboard traversal with visible focus
a11y_i18n.body: A test that tabs through each page and asserts every interactive element is reachable exactly once, with a focus ring that meets contrast.

a11y_i18n.title: Screen-reader announcements for live updates
a11y_i18n.body: The finder does this; extend it to votes, tallies and feed refreshes, with aria-live regions that announce outcomes, not raw JSON.

a11y_i18n.title: Localisation infrastructure with one real second language
a11y_i18n.body: Message files, a language switch, plural and date handling — and at least one fully translated locale, because a half-built i18n layer rots.

a11y_i18n.title: Right-to-left layout support
a11y_i18n.body: Logical CSS properties, mirrored chevrons and a test that flips dir=rtl and asserts no overflow.

a11y_i18n.title: Plain-language mode
a11y_i18n.body: A toggle that shortens sentences and defines jargon inline, generated from the glossary, for readers who are not native speakers.

a11y_i18n.title: Colour-blind safe status encoding
a11y_i18n.body: Status is colour plus shape plus text everywhere, with a test that greps for colour-only styling.

a11y_i18n.title: Respect prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-contrast
a11y_i18n.body: Every animation and gradient behind those media queries, with a test page listing what changes.

a11y_i18n.title: Alt text enforced at upload
a11y_i18n.body: An image without a description is refused or marked decorative explicitly, because 'add alt text later' never happens.

a11y_i18n.title: Error messages that say what to do next
a11y_i18n.body: Every 4xx page gets an action line and a link, and a test asserts no error page lacks one.

a11y_i18n.title: A reading level measured in CI
a11y_i18n.body: A simple readability score on user-facing help text, failing above a stated threshold.

a11y_i18n.title: Translated taxonomy labels
a11y_i18n.body: The categories and themes are English strings in the database; a translation table keeps the schema and translates the labels.

a11y_i18n.title: A language-aware search that does not split on accents
a11y_i18n.body: Stemming and diacritic folding per locale, with a test per language the site claims to support.

performance.title: Budget the page weight and fail the build over it
performance.body: A stated kB budget per page type, measured in the e2e run, so the site cannot drift into 400 kB of JavaScript one feature at a time.

performance.title: Cache every read route that has no session dependency
performance.body: Public project pages change rarely; an ETag plus a short TTL removes most database work from the hot path.

performance.title: N+1 detection in the test suite
performance.body: Count queries per request in tests and assert a ceiling per route, which is how an N+1 is caught before it becomes a 300 ms page.

performance.title: Cursor pagination everywhere
performance.body: Offset pagination degrades and duplicates rows under writes; the feeds and search should share one cursor implementation.

performance.title: A slow-query log with a stated threshold
performance.body: Anything over 50 ms recorded with its route and its plan, reviewed weekly.

performance.title: Precompute the instance-wide aggregates on a schedule
performance.body: Pain scores and health are recomputed per request today; a snapshot table makes the expensive numbers cheap and comparable over time.

performance.title: Compress and fingerprint every asset
performance.body: Stable hashed filenames with long cache lifetimes; the asset helper already versions by query string, which busts caches on every deploy.

performance.title: Lazy-load the panels that are below the fold
performance.body: The project page fetches six panels on load; three of them are never seen by most readers.

performance.title: A load profile that runs on every release
performance.body: A recorded scenario (browse, search, vote) replayed against a seeded database, with the p95 compared to the last release.

performance.title: Indexes justified by query plans in CI
performance.body: A test asserting each documented hot query uses an index, so a schema change cannot silently drop one.

performance.title: Stream the export instead of buffering
performance.body: A large project export currently builds in memory; chunked streaming keeps it alive on a small host.

performance.title: Debounce and cancel in-flight searches
performance.body: Typing in the search box issues a request per keystroke; an AbortController plus a delay cuts the load by an order of magnitude.

performance.title: A cold-start measurement for the server
performance.body: Time to first successful request after a restart, tracked per release, because this instance restarts on every deploy.

security.title: Two-factor authentication with recovery codes
security.body: TOTP plus ten single-use codes, shown once, with an audit row for enrolment and for each use.

security.title: Session list with remote revocation
security.body: Every session visible with its last-seen IP and agent, and a revoke button that actually invalidates the token server-side.

security.title: Password breach checks against k-anonymised ranges
security.body: Refuse a password found in a breach corpus without sending the password anywhere, using the range API.

security.title: Rate limits keyed on identity as well as address
security.body: The limiter keys on IP today; an authenticated abuser on a shared address is invisible. Key on account with a separate, higher budget.

security.title: CSRF tokens on every state-changing form
security.body: One middleware, a per-session token in every form and header, and a test that a forged request is refused.

security.title: A security policy with a disclosure route and a response clock
security.body: SECURITY.md, a contact, a stated acknowledgement time, and a page recording disclosures and fixes.

security.title: Content Security Policy without unsafe-inline
security.body: The current policy allows inline script; moving to nonces removes the main XSS amplifier and is testable by asserting the header per page.

security.title: Per-project visibility enforced in one place with a test matrix
security.body: Private, unlisted, protected and public each get a table of who may read what, and a test per cell — the current enforcement is spread across handlers.

security.title: Audit every read of a private project
security.body: Nobody can see who looked at a private project today; if it is private, access should leave a trace.

security.title: Encrypted backups
security.body: A backup on the same disk as the database is a copy, not a backup; encrypt off-host copies and document the key handling.

security.title: Dependency and image scanning in CI
security.body: Vulnerability scan on every build with a stated severity policy for failing.

security.title: Secrets that cannot reach the logs
security.body: A redaction layer on the logger plus a test that feeds a token-shaped string through every log path.

security.title: Login anomaly notices
security.body: A new country or a new user agent sends one notice, with a link to revoke, and never blocks.

integrations.title: A GitHub webhook that records events without a second database
integrations.body: The forge_events table exists for this; wire push, PR, review and comment so newcomer responsiveness can be measured from real data.

integrations.title: A two-way issue mirror for linked features
integrations.body: A shipped feature opens an issue in the repository and closes it when the field report says it worked, with the mapping stored.

integrations.title: CI status shown on the feature page
integrations.body: A feature's branch and its last CI result, read from the forge API, so 'is it done?' stops being a status field somebody edits.

integrations.title: A Slack/Discord bridge for decisions
integrations.body: Ratified decisions post to a channel with a link, one message per decision, configurable per project.

integrations.title: Generic outbound webhooks with signing
integrations.body: Any consumer can subscribe to decision, ship and complaint events, with an HMAC signature header and retry with backoff.

integrations.title: An import from GitHub or GitLab issues
integrations.body: Point at a repository and turn its issues into complaints with the reporter and the URL preserved, so a project can migrate its pain.

integrations.title: A CLI that files complaints and lists work from a terminal
integrations.body: One static binary using the existing API, for maintainers who live in a shell.

integrations.title: A browser extension that files a complaint from any page
integrations.body: The report-this-project path is manual today; an extension captures the URL and opens the form pre-filled.

integrations.title: Syndication to my own site via a static build
integrations.body: A generator that reads the public API and produces a static mirror of a project's public pages.

integrations.title: Email-in complaints
integrations.body: A dedicated address per project that accepts a message and files it, with the sender verified by SPF and a reply-by-email thread.

integrations.title: Calendar feeds for decision deadlines
integrations.body: An iCal feed per project of voting windows that close, so nobody misses a quorum because of a timezone.

integrations.title: A single sign-on option for the instance's other sites
integrations.body: The network already shares an identity in practice; one OIDC provider removes a fourth password.

mobile.title: A real PWA with offline reading
mobile.body: Service-worker caching of the pages a reader follows, an install prompt that appears after engagement, and an offline page that says what is unavailable.

mobile.title: Thumb-reachable primary actions on mobile
mobile.body: The vote and claim controls sit at the top of the viewport; a mobile layout puts the three primary actions in a bottom bar.

mobile.title: A share sheet integration
mobile.body: Sharing a decision produces a link with OpenGraph metadata and a one-line summary, so the receiving app shows something better than a bare URL.

mobile.title: Mobile-first board columns
mobile.body: The kanban is horizontally scrolled on a phone; a stacked column view with a status switcher replaces it below 640 px.

mobile.title: Tap targets and text at accessible sizes
mobile.body: A test asserting every interactive element is at least 44 px and body text at least 16 px at 375 px width.

mobile.title: Native share targets for install
mobile.body: Web app manifest with icons, screenshots and a start URL per surface, so the installed app opens the feed rather than the home page.

mobile.title: Pull-to-refresh on the feeds
mobile.body: One gesture, with a visible timestamp of the last successful fetch.

mobile.title: Offline draft persistence
mobile.body: A complaint written on a train survives the tunnel; drafts are stored locally and offered for resume.

mobile.title: Camera capture for screenshots in a complaint
mobile.body: Evidence is the difference between a vague complaint and a fixable one; a file input with capture and a size cap.

mobile.title: A compact density mode
mobile.body: For people who scan a lot on a phone: less padding, more rows, remembered per device.

mobile.title: Push notifications on install
mobile.body: The same web push subscription, requested at install time with the reason stated.

mobile.title: App shortcuts in the manifest
mobile.body: Long-press an icon to jump to file-a-complaint or the contribution feed.

mobile.title: A mobile e2e profile in CI
mobile.body: The Playwright suites run at desktop width only; a 375 px project runs the same assertions.

ui_depth.title: One design-token source for colour, spacing and type
ui_depth.body: The CSS repeats hex values in a dozen files; a token layer plus a test that forbids raw hex outside it makes a theme change one edit.

ui_depth.title: A dark and light theme generated from the same tokens
ui_depth.body: With a contrast assertion per token pair, so 'dark mode' cannot ship a 2.1:1 label.

ui_depth.title: Per-project accent colour chosen by the owner
ui_depth.body: A small, bounded palette so a project is recognisable in a list without breaking contrast rules.

ui_depth.title: Dense and comfortable table modes
ui_depth.body: Two row heights on every list, remembered per member, because a table that suits a laptop is unusable on a projector.

ui_depth.title: A command palette with every route and action
ui_depth.body: Ctrl-K over routes, projects and actions, built from the router's own table so it cannot list a page that does not exist.

ui_depth.title: Inline editing everywhere with the same component
ui_depth.body: Titles and bodies are editable in place on some pages and behind a form on others; one component, one keyboard contract.

ui_depth.title: Undo for destructive actions instead of a confirm dialog
ui_depth.body: A toast with a five-second undo backed by a soft delete, replacing the modal that everyone clicks through.

ui_depth.title: A real empty state for every panel
ui_depth.body: Each panel explains what would fill it and links to the action that starts it — the current mix of blank boxes and 'no data' is the most visible thinness.

ui_depth.title: Skeletons that match the final layout
ui_depth.body: Loaders currently reserve the wrong height, so the page jumps; one skeleton per panel type.

ui_depth.title: A comparison view for two competing solutions
ui_depth.body: The arena asks for a judgement; a side-by-side view with the complaints each answers makes the judgement informed rather than a coin flip.

ui_depth.title: Print stylesheets for decisions and specs
ui_depth.body: A decision record should print legibly on one page; today it prints the navigation twice.

ui_depth.title: Progress indicators that state the scale
ui_depth.body: A bar with no denominator is decoration; every progress bar names its total and its unit.

ui_depth.title: An activity timeline per project
ui_depth.body: One reverse-chronological stream of filings, validations, ships and decisions, filterable, replacing four separate lists.

ui_depth.title: Keyboard-visible focus order that follows visual order
ui_depth.body: A test asserting DOM order matches visual order on each page, because tab order that jumps is a maze for keyboard users.

ai.title: Draft the complaint body from a title
ai.body: A model expands a one-line title into a structured complaint the filer then edits, cutting the most common quality problem at its source.

ai.title: Suggest the complaint a feature answers
ai.body: On feature creation, rank the candidate complaints by similarity and show the top three with their pain scores, so an unlinked feature becomes linked.

ai.title: Cluster duplicate complaints nightly, propose merges
ai.body: A batch job writes merge proposals with the members listed; a human approves. Never auto-merge.

ai.title: Summarise a long thread into the decision record
ai.body: The ratified decision gets an extractive-then-generated summary that cites the comments it used, and the citations are checked before rendering.

ai.title: Translate a complaint into the maintainer's language
ai.body: On-demand translation of complaint bodies with the original always visible and the model named.

ai.title: Detect a complaint that is actually a feature request
ai.body: Classify on filing and offer the correct form with the text preserved, instead of letting it rot in the wrong queue.

ai.title: Flag feature proposals that restate shipped work
ai.body: Similarity against shipped features at filing time, with links, which is the cheapest way to stop a backlog re-litigating the past.

ai.title: Estimate effort from comparable past features
ai.body: Retrieve the nearest shipped features and report their actual claim-to-close time as an evidence-based size suggestion.

ai.title: An assistant that answers 'what does this project decide?'
ai.body: Retrieval over the spec, decisions and documents with citations to sections, refusing when the corpus has no answer.

ai.title: Moderation triage that ranks reports by likely severity
ai.body: A model-assisted queue ordering with the reason shown, and every decision still made by a human whose name is on it.

ai.title: Accessibility description suggestions for uploaded images
ai.body: A suggested alt text the uploader must confirm or edit, so the field is never left empty.

ai.title: A weekly generated digest reviewed by a human before sending
ai.body: Draft, preview, edit, send — the model writes, a person signs.

ai.title: Prompt and model versioning with a fallback
ai.body: Every model call records the prompt version and model, and a failure falls back to the non-AI path rather than an error page.

ai.title: A hard rule: no AI content is published without a label
ai.body: Anything model-drafted carries a visible marker and an audit row, including after a human edits it.

federation.title: ActivityPub outbox for projects
federation.body: A project publishes its decisions and ships as ActivityPub activities, so a Mastodon user can follow it without an account here.

federation.title: An inbox that accepts follows and replies
federation.body: Handle Follow, Undo and Create at least minimally, with the actor mapped to a project or a member.

federation.title: WebFinger and nodeinfo
federation.body: Two small endpoints that make the instance discoverable and described to the wider fediverse.

federation.title: Cross-instance project identity
federation.body: Two instances could describe the same project; a canonical URL and a claim flow would let the catalogs merge rather than duplicate.

federation.title: Federated complaints with provenance
federation.body: A complaint received from another instance keeps its origin and its reporter's instance shown, so local weight is not granted by default.

federation.title: A static mirror for the small-web
federation.body: Publish each project as plain HTML on a static host, regenerated on ship — the site survives its own server being down.

federation.title: IndieAuth or a rel=me verification for member profiles
federation.body: A member can prove a personal site is theirs, which makes external identity a first-class thing rather than a bio link.

federation.title: Webmention for discussions elsewhere
federation.body: A blog post linking a decision sends a webmention that appears as a linked reference on the decision page.

federation.title: An export designed to be re-hosted
federation.body: The portability export plus a static generator equals a portable instance; document the minimal viable re-host.

federation.title: A public instance directory of Concord instances
federation.body: Which instances exist, their governance models and their catalogs, so the network is visible rather than asserted.

federation.title: Signed instance identity
federation.body: A keypair per instance and signed exports, so a mirrored catalog can be verified rather than trusted.

federation.title: Federated search with privacy-preserving queries
federation.body: Ask several instances for counts, not results, and fetch only what the reader chooses.

federation.title: A bridge that mirrors a project's decisions into a wiki
federation.body: Any MediaWiki or Outline instance can consume the same feed; the bridge is configuration, not code.

analytics.title: A funnel from visit to first contribution
analytics.body: Five steps, counted server-side with no personal identifiers, so 'is onboarding working?' has an answer that is not a guess.

analytics.title: Decision throughput per week, with the trend
analytics.body: Calls opened versus decided per week, and the median time in each state — the single chart that says whether governance is functioning.

analytics.title: Complaint to ship lead time, by project and by theme
analytics.body: The number a user feels; publish it with its sample size and its outliers named rather than smoothed away.

analytics.title: Search success rate as a first-class metric
analytics.body: Share of searches that lead to a click within the session, and the top zero-result queries, reviewed weekly.

analytics.title: Retention cohorts without tracking individuals
analytics.body: Weekly cohorts counted as aggregates on first-visit week, with a k-anonymity floor, and no per-user event log.

analytics.title: A public metrics page generated from the database
analytics.body: Instance-level counts (projects, complaints, decisions, ships) rendered from the same queries the stats API serves.

analytics.title: Experiment flags with a stated expiry
analytics.body: A flag registry where every flag has an owner and an end date, and the build fails when one expires — the only way flags do not become permanent branches.

analytics.title: A/B results recorded as decisions
analytics.body: When an experiment concludes, its outcome becomes a decision record with the evidence, so the learning outlives the code.

analytics.title: Which complaints predicted impact
analytics.body: Compare a complaint's severity and frequency with the field-report outcome of the fix; publish the correlation so severity means something.

analytics.title: Dead-page detection from the access log
analytics.body: Routes nobody visits for a quarter appear in a report, because an unused surface is either broken or unnecessary.

analytics.title: Cost per decision
analytics.body: Hosting and operational cost divided by decisions made per month: a governance number nobody computes but everyone should see.

analytics.title: An anomaly alert on sudden drops
analytics.body: Ships per week or decisions per week falling below a stated band raises one alert to the operator, not a dashboard nobody opens.

community.title: Credit contributors on the ship they made
community.body: The feature page names who validated, who voted and who shipped, with the role each played, not just the author.

community.title: A contributor's public portfolio page
community.body: What they filed, validated, shipped and decided, exportable and linkable — the thing a contributor actually wants to show.

community.title: Thank-you notes that are not gamified badges
community.body: A single, rate-limited appreciation per person per month, displayed on their page; no streak counters, no leaderboard of hours.

community.title: A monthly 'state of the instance' post, generated
community.body: Decisions, ships, new projects and one thing that went badly, assembled from the data with a short human preamble.

community.title: Office hours as a recurring, timezone-rotated event
community.body: Two slots a month at different hours, with an agenda built from the open complaints in a theme.

community.title: Mentor matching with an explicit opt-in
community.body: Mentors state the areas and the hours they can give; newcomers request a session; both sides get a calendar link and no obligation beyond it.

community.title: First-contribution celebration that names the work
community.body: One notification on the first merged contribution naming the project and the maintainer who responded, because the second contribution depends on it.

community.title: Project maintainer office hours in the contribution feed
community.body: The feed shows 'this project is answering questions Thursday' as a work item, so help-seeking is a task a newcomer can do.

community.title: A 'we need you here' list per project
community.body: Which roles are unfilled, with the requirements stated, so a reader can see exactly how to be useful rather than generally volunteering.

community.title: Recognition for review, not only for code
community.body: Response times and review counts are contributions; show them on the same portfolio page as the ships.

community.title: A leaving page that asks one question
community.body: When someone deletes an account, one optional question with fixed answers, aggregated and published — the only reliable source of why people leave.

community.title: Local meetups listed per project
community.body: A date, a place and a link; no ticketing, no integration, just a surface that says people meet.

meta_quality.title: Every claim in the README re-checked by CI
meta_quality.body: Counts, test numbers and feature lists in the docs are asserted by the doc-numbers gate; extend the same discipline to the README's claims.

meta_quality.title: A public status page fed by real probes
meta_quality.body: Health, last deploy, last successful healthsync, last backup, with the timestamps exposed on a page rather than in a journal.

meta_quality.title: Green-not-broken: a failing test cannot merge
meta_quality.body: The repository's own gate discipline applied to the instance: a documented rule that no deploy ships with a red gate, and a script that refuses it.

meta_quality.title: Property-based tests for the ranking engine
meta_quality.body: The pairwise model has invariants (a self-vote never counts, ratings stay bounded, order is deterministic) that a property test proves over random input.

meta_quality.title: A mutation score published per package
meta_quality.body: The gates already compute killed/total; publishing the per-package score turns coverage into a number people can compete on sensibly.

meta_quality.title: Fuzz the API with a grammar of valid bodies
meta_quality.body: Most 500s come from shapes nobody typed; a fuzzer over the OpenAPI schema finds them without a user.

meta_quality.title: A regression corpus for reported bugs
meta_quality.body: Every fixed bug leaves one minimal test with the issue link in its name, so the same class of bug cannot return silently.

meta_quality.title: Restore drills with a measured RTO
meta_quality.body: A scheduled job restores yesterday's backup into a scratch database and runs the smoke suite against it.

meta_quality.title: An incident log with postmortems
meta_quality.body: One page per incident: impact, timeline, cause, what changed. The absence of this page is why incidents repeat.

meta_quality.title: Dependency upgrade policy with an automated PR
meta_quality.body: Weekly automated upgrade PRs that the gates judge, with a stated policy for majors.

meta_quality.title: A benchmark of the mutation gate's own sensitivity
meta_quality.body: Inject a known-untested function and assert the gate reports a survivor; a gate that cannot fail is a gate nobody should trust.

meta_quality.title: Documentation for every public API route, generated
meta_quality.body: The router's table rendered as an OpenAPI document, with a test that a route without a description fails the build.

meta_quality.title: A quarterly architecture review recorded as a decision
meta_quality.body: One decision record per quarter reviewing the module graph, the dependency rules and the known debt, so the architecture has a history rather than a legend.

intake_modes.title: Per-project intake mode: complaint-first, idea-first, or both
intake_modes.body: `projects` gains `intake_mode` CHECKed to `complaint_first|idea_first|both`, defaulting to `complaint_first` so a deploy changes no existing project's behaviour. Read at the one place that enforces the rule (`CreateFeature`) and echoed by the new-idea form, so the product has one answer to "may I file an idea here?"

intake_modes.title: Let a feature be created without a complaint when the mode allows it
intake_modes.body: `CreateFeature` refuses an empty linked-complaint set today with a message about the requirement rather than the project's policy. Make the guard mode-aware and make the refusal name the mode and the route to change it, instead of a rule the reader cannot look up.

intake_modes.title: Prove that an idea-first feature still ranks
intake_modes.body: The shipped copy says an unlinked feature "ranks on nothing", which is a claim about the ranking that no code enforces: `/ranking` reads `features.elo_r` directly and never touches complaints. Either make the sentence true or delete it, and add the test that holds whichever answer is chosen, because a doc claim about ranking is a claim about a number readers act on.

intake_modes.title: Acquire-a-complaint gate before a feature reaches ready
intake_modes.body: Idea-first intake still ends at a commitment only when someone has felt the pain. Let `ready` require at least one validated complaint unless the project's mode is `idea_first`, and put the refusal in the status transition where the other §6.2 rules already live -- not in a second checker.

intake_modes.title: Convert a feature between complaint-backed and idea-first, as an act
intake_modes.body: Features filed before a mode change, and ideas that later acquire pain, both need the other shape. A link/unlink act with an `audit_log` row, reversible the way moderation is (a second act, not a mutated row), so the project's ledger can show how a given idea got its evidence.

intake_modes.title: Show the intake mode where a reader files
intake_modes.body: The form that asks for a complaint should say whether the project requires one. Render the project's mode on the new-idea form and on the overview beside the governance model, both of which already load the project -- this is a template change, not a query.

intake_modes.title: Badge the evidence: complaint-backed versus idea-first
intake_modes.body: A reader judging an idea needs to know whether somebody suffered it or somebody liked it. One badge in the features list and one line on the feature page, read from the same linked-complaint count the page already loads.

intake_modes.title: Changing the intake mode is a proposal, not a maintainer dial
intake_modes.body: The mode decides whose work counts as legitimate input, which is a charter question rather than a setting. Route it through the curation queue as a new proposal kind so it inherits the existing consent, quorum and audit machinery instead of a bespoke endpoint.

intake_modes.title: Evidence alternatives: a document or a field report instead of a complaint
intake_modes.body: Some ideas answer a written spec section or a field report rather than a complaint. Let the evidence requirement be satisfied by one of the three, with the same validation rule, so a project documenting itself does not have to restate its own spec as pain.

intake_modes.title: Intake-mode changes as their own audit kind
intake_modes.body: An `intake` kind on the modlog, resolved through the store vocabulary the way `moderation` already is. Bundled with the proposal kind above it is redundant; alone it is a filter over rows nobody searches for yet.

milestones.title: A milestones table with a target date and a status
milestones.body: `milestones(id, project_id, title, body, target_date, status CHECK(planned|active|done|cancelled), created_at)` with `UNIQUE(project_id, title)`. Nullable `target_date`, because a milestone dated by wish is a deadline nobody agreed to. Append-only migration `0036`.

milestones.title: features.milestone_id, nullable, indexed
milestones.body: One nullable FK plus `CREATE INDEX features_milestone ON features(milestone_id)`. Nullable is the whole design: a backlog is the set of features no milestone claims, and a default milestone would make that set unrepresentable.

milestones.title: The milestone page: its features, grouped by status
milestones.body: `/projects/{slug}/milestones/{id}` reusing the existing status grouping and the same counts the board computes, plus progress as closed/total. A page whose only job is to show one group is cheap; the value is that every later surface links to something.

milestones.title: Assign and unassign from the feature page
milestones.body: `PUT /api/v1/projects/{slug}/features/{id}/milestone` with `{milestone_id|null}`, gated on the project's role ladder. Unassigning must be as easy as assigning, or the first wrong click is permanent until a database edit.

milestones.title: Filter the board by milestone
milestones.body: A `milestone` query parameter on the board read, composing with the existing phase filter. One board, filtered -- not a board per milestone, which would fork the WIP limits and the card placement rules.

milestones.title: Milestone progress that cannot be an import artefact
milestones.body: Closed-over-total is the same trap instance statistics already fell into: 925 of 1,874 features have no creation event, so a progress bar computed from `status` alone measures a seeding script. Derive it from status transitions that carry an audit row, and show the provenance split beside it.

milestones.title: Closing a milestone: unfinished work carries forward, one act per feature
milestones.body: A `done` milestone with open features is a lie; a blocked close is a trap. Move them to a named successor with an audit act each, so "why did this feature move" is answerable from the log rather than from memory.

milestones.title: At-risk flag when the target date has passed with open features
milestones.body: Derived, never stored: `target_date < now() AND open > 0`. Storing it would need a job to keep it true, and a stale "on track" badge is worse than no badge.

milestones.title: A consensus call over a milestone as one unit
milestones.body: §6.2's calls are per feature. A milestone is the size at which a maintainer actually asks for consent, and the existing call machinery already handles eligibility, quorum and the hidden tally -- the work is the many-to-one mapping, not the rules.

milestones.title: Hand-ordered milestones with drag reordering
milestones.body: `position` per project and a drag handle. Ordered by `target_date` already answers it, and hand order is a second ordering to keep in sync with the dates the moment either changes.

roadmap_view.title: A roadmap page with milestones on a timeline
roadmap_view.body: `/projects/{slug}/roadmap` renders each milestone as a column with its features grouped by status, ordered by target date, and works with zero milestones (the empty state names what to create rather than apologising).

roadmap_view.title: A roadmap read route
roadmap_view.body: `GET /api/v1/projects/{slug}/roadmap` returning milestones with their counts, so the page and any third party read one shape. Every page in this repo that computes its own numbers is one page whose numbers can disagree with the route's.

roadmap_view.title: Slippage: planned versus shipped per milestone
roadmap_view.body: For each closed milestone, the hours between target date and the last shipment, and for each open one the age of its oldest open feature. This is the number a roadmap is for, and it is computable from `audit_log` plus `target_date` with no new storage.

roadmap_view.title: The next milestone on the project overview
roadmap_view.body: One line naming the earliest open milestone and its remaining count, on the page a reader actually lands on. The roadmap page is for people who already decided to look; this is for the ones who did not.

roadmap_view.title: A feed item when a milestone opens or closes
