roadmap_view.body: The project feed already publishes decisions; a plan changing is a decision. One item per transition, through the existing feed writer rather than a second one.

roadmap_view.title: A milestone badge SVG
roadmap_view.body: The instance badge already answers "what is this project". A second SVG for the current milestone is another endpoint to keep alive for a surface that mostly appears in READMEs nobody re-reads.

roadmap_view.title: Generate the roadmap by parsing docs/PLAN-r4.md
roadmap_view.body: A doc parser as the source of the roadmap makes the document the schema. The instance should own the plan and the document should describe it, or the two disagree the first time somebody edits prose.

roadmap_view.title: iCal export of milestone target dates
roadmap_view.body: A calendar feed implies the dates are commitments. Until slippage is measured, exporting them advertises a schedule the project cannot keep.

scheduling.title: Feature dependencies: blocks and blocked_by
scheduling.body: `feature_deps(blocker_id, blocked_id)` with both FKs and a unique pair. A feature with an open blocker refuses `in_progress` at the same transition that already enforces the §6.2 rules, so the constraint exists where work moves rather than in a report nobody reads.

scheduling.title: A blocked badge with the blocking feature named
scheduling.body: In the list and on the card: the count of open blockers, and on the feature page their titles. A dependency nobody can see is a dependency that gets ignored until the day it bites.

scheduling.title: Bulk assign a selection of features to a milestone
scheduling.body: Multi-select in the features list, one `PUT .../milestone` per feature in one transaction. Grouping 130 ideas one page-load at a time is what makes people keep their plan in a spreadsheet.

scheduling.title: Order the features inside a milestone
scheduling.body: `position` on the milestone-feature relationship, not on the feature, because the same feature can be third in one milestone and last in another. Reorder via drag, persisted as integers with gaps.

scheduling.title: Milestone-scoped WIP: the board's limits read the milestone's size
scheduling.body: `board_columns.wip_limit` is fixed per project (3 in progress, 4 in review) and takes no account of how much a milestone contains. Show the milestone's share of each column beside the limit, which is a read, not a second limit to enforce.

scheduling.title: Refuse a dependency cycle, naming the cycle
scheduling.body: A depth-first walk on insert returning the path found, so the refusal is `a blocks b blocks a` rather than `invalid`. Two nodes and a shared blocker is the shape that ships without it.

scheduling.title: Place a card for every new feature
scheduling.body: Measured after this list was first written, and it refutes the idea: `GetBoard` returns a DERIVED card for every feature, so all 332 already appear in `inbox`; `board_cards` holds 20 rows because a row is written only when somebody MOVES a card (that is what `?feature_id=` on `PUT /board/cards/0/move` is for). Seeding a row per feature would therefore duplicate what the renderer already derives and would make "placed" mean nothing. The real gap the measurement found is smaller and different: a derived card and a placed row are indistinguishable to a reader, and neither is in the API's response as such.

scheduling.title: Milestone-scoped board columns
scheduling.body: A board per milestone, each with its own phases. Two boards over one backlog means two answers to "what phase is this in", and the filter above delivers the useful part of this for a fraction of the cost.

scheduling.title: A dependency graph view
scheduling.body: Nodes and edges for a project's features rendered in SVG. Pretty, and the blocked badge plus the refusal already prevent the harm; this shows the shape to people who already know it.

scheduling.title: Auto-assign new features to the current milestone
scheduling.body: A per-project toggle that puts every new feature in the active milestone. It makes the backlog unrepresentable -- the set no milestone claims is exactly what a backlog is -- and a mode change is the cheaper way to express the intent.

shipped.title: Complaint-first development
shipped.body: Every feature must answer a validated complaint; an unlinked feature ranks on nothing. Complaints carry severity, frequency and a strategic multiplier.

shipped.title: Pairwise ranking with Glicko-2
shipped.body: Features and solutions are ranked by judged pairwise comparisons, with rating deviation and volatility, not by star counts or upvote totals.

shipped.title: Consensus with quorum, blocks and an override window
shipped.body: Calls close on quorum, a standing block can hold them, and a second window lets a block be overridden with a written remedy.

shipped.title: Decision records
shipped.body: Every closed call writes a record: the alternatives, the tally, the agreed fallback and the date, linked from the feature.

shipped.title: Trust and reputation events
shipped.body: Contribution events carry points, roles are granted with a reason, and guest accounts can be folded into a real account without losing rows.

shipped.title: Kanban board with phase gates
shipped.body: Draft to ready to in-progress to shipped, with the gates that stop a feature skipping a phase.

shipped.title: Audit ledger
shipped.body: Every privileged action writes a row that cannot be edited; the ledger is the trust anchor for everything else.

shipped.title: Documents, lists and requests
shipped.body: Long-form documents, curated lists and a public request board, each with its own routes and readers.

shipped.title: Taxonomy, themes and criteria
shipped.body: Categories, strategic themes with consensus-ratified weights, and criteria profiles evaluated per project.

shipped.title: Search with facets and a query language
shipped.body: tag:, language:, NOT, phrase search, facets per dimension, and a relevance sort that is explainable.

shipped.title: Embedding-based duplicate detection
shipped.body: Near-identical complaints and features are detected at filing time and shown as an advisory warning rather than a refusal.

shipped.title: Arena and alternatives
shipped.body: Competing solutions to one complaint are judged in pairs, with an arena weight and a verification path.

shipped.title: Field reports and capabilities
shipped.body: People who used a shipped solution report whether it worked, weighted by reputation; capabilities are confirmed by more than one reporter.

shipped.title: Finder
shipped.body: A session-based question flow that narrows the catalog by information gain, with gaps shown when no question is worth asking.

shipped.title: Merge gate and redirects
shipped.body: Duplicate projects can be merged with their rows moved and their slug redirected, rather than deleted.

shipped.title: Guest accounts and consent
shipped.body: Anonymous participation with a consent state that is decided server-side on first paint.

shipped.title: Arenas
shipped.body: Judged pairs of alternative solutions, with an arena weight and a verification path.

shipped.title: Solutions
shipped.body: A solution answers one or more complaints and can be judged against a rival.

shipped.title: Solution ranking and coverage
shipped.body: Ranked solutions with a coverage claim that says which complaints a solution answers.

shipped.title: Ranking feeding consensus
shipped.body: The ranking gates which alternatives reach a call, so a call is a decision among ranked options.

shipped.title: Field reports and capabilities
shipped.body: Outcome reports from people who used a solution, plus confirmed capabilities per project.

shipped.title: Scout
shipped.body: Ask whether a project should exist: a structured interrogation with a verdict and its reasoning.

shipped.title: Administration surface
shipped.body: Visibility, tags, languages and invites on the settings page, with the read halves that were missing.

shipped.title: Repository identity and health ingest
shipped.body: Canonical repository URLs per project, a forgeseed command that refuses an incomplete mapping, and an hourly ingest that measures recency, breadth, cadence and review latency -- with unknown distinct from zero.

shipped.title: Work-item contract
shipped.body: Difficulty, an optional time budget, needs-mentor and a claim with a partial unique index, exposed as the work-items API and a project panel.

shipped.title: Contribution feed
shipped.body: Open work items filtered by language, time budget, difficulty and mentor, ranked through the Finder engine and a project-health tiebreak, on a server-rendered page.

planned.title: Newcomer responsiveness
planned.body: Median hours to a first response for a first-time pull-request author, published only with its sample size and never folded into the health score.

planned.title: Census with a provenance split
planned.body: Composition of the instance with seeded rows separated from organic ones, because 925 of 1,874 features have no creation event and a growth chart of those is a chart of one import.

planned.title: Decision latency and exposure
planned.body: Three medians -- complaint to validation, ready to shipped, call opened to closed -- each with its n and its unfinished count, plus a stats page, SVG badges and a feed item.

planned.title: Snapshot history and derived surfaces
planned.body: A daily snapshot table, a 90-day history route, and only then rising trends and a responsiveness leaderboard.

planned.title: Documentation sync
planned.body: Keep the specs, the plan and the remaining-work log in step with the code as a gate rather than a habit. In progress.

planned.title: Repository mapping
planned.body: Sixty-nine of seventy-four catalog projects have no stated repository, so they cannot be measured; the mapping is an owner decision, not an implementation step.
